confidence_note: Book text not read; principle wording from the authors' site and Wikipedia. Old text's 'babies cry when hungry', 'brain evolved to produce signals', and the 8 pm rule were not found and are omitted. Concept with no anecdote.
facts: Honor your hunger: meet your body's energy needs so extreme hunger does not take over, and respond to early hunger cues to rebuild trust with food.
Feel your fullness: notice when hunger fades and you become comfortably full; pause during meals to check how the food tastes and how full you feel.
Discover the satisfaction factor: enjoyment is a valid goal of eating; eating foods you truly want in a pleasant setting helps you feel content with smaller amounts.
The approach works through body awareness, called interoceptive awareness, and is not a diet or food plan; it has no pass-or-fail rules.
Critics note the lack of a set plan can make it hard to know what and how much to eat, and learning to read cues has a steep learning curve.
Observational studies link it to less overeating and better self-regulation but cannot show cause.
scene_details: a pause halfway through a meal
tension: The authors want you to rebuild trust in hunger and fullness signals while giving no rule to follow, which critics say makes it hard to learn.
opening_idea: Two of the ten principles concern signals dieters tend to override.

lessons.idea: Check in with hunger before and during a meal.
lessons.anchor: the pause halfway through to check taste and fullness

reflect_final: At which meal this week could you stop halfway for a moment to check how the food tastes and how full you are?

use_cases.move: Stop halfway and check whether you still want it and how full you are.

use_cases.situation: A child is told to finish the plate
use_cases.move: Let them take what they want and say when they are full.

use_cases.situation: Ordering at a restaurant out of habit
use_cases.move: Pick what you actually want and check how you feel halfway.

pocket_idea: Eat when the first hunger signal arrives, and pause halfway to ask how it tastes and how full you are.

conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Honor hunger early, pause to feel fullness, add satisfaction, with the caveat of learning curve.
